analysis.coverage.description: Emits UNKNOWN when a required least-privilege identity collection for a scanned scope is missing or has a status other than collected or empty; account-global AWS IAM collections can cover regional scopes of that account. It also reports malformed native facts caught during per-resource or Azure assignment review and allowed grants whose permission criticality is unknown or partial. No PASS or FAIL is emitted by this check.
evaluated: resource.data passed to per-resource grant, usage, principal and network-rule review
analysis.coverage.pass_when: Never emits PASS. Complete required least-privilege collections and classifiable, well-formed evaluated facts produce no coverage finding.
analysis.coverage.fail_when: Never emits FAIL. A required least-privilege collection gap, caught malformed fact, or allowed non-broad grant with unknown or partially classified criticality emits UNKNOWN.
analysis.coverage.not_applicable_when: No coverage finding is emitted when the applicable least-privilege collection statuses are collected or empty (including covered AWS account-global IAM inventory) and no malformed review facts or unclassified allowed grants are encountered.

analysis.federated_trust.description: Reviews AWS IAM role web-identity trust, active GCP workload identity providers, and Azure managed-identity or directory-application federated credentials. AWS requires a positive issuer sub condition except for Cognito, which requires aud; broad subject wildcards fail. A known multi-tenant GCP OIDC issuer without attributeCondition fails. Azure claim-expression wildcards fail only when the issuer-specific subject pinning test considers them broad. Other weak or unresolved configurations may yield MANUAL or UNKNOWN.
evaluated: resource.provider and resource.type: AWS iam_role, GCP workload_identity_provider, Azure managed_identity_federated_credential or directory_application_federated_credential
analysis.federated_trust.pass_when: An applicable AWS web-identity trust has no serious subject or Cognito audience problem and no review-only guest Cognito issue; a GCP provider has any truthy attributeCondition; or an Azure credential has a subject or claim expression without a broad wildcard. A missing GitHub aud condition alone is recorded as a low-severity problem but does not prevent PASS.
analysis.federated_trust.fail_when: AWS lacks a positive sub condition, has a broad positive Like sub value, or has Cognito trust without a positive aud condition; a known multi-tenant GCP OIDC issuer has no attributeCondition; or an Azure claims expression contains a wildcard judged broad by the issuer-specific pinning test.
analysis.federated_trust.not_applicable_when: No finding for an AWS role without an applicable Allow web-identity statement (SAML principals are skipped), a deleted or disabled GCP provider, or a resource outside the four handled types. A missing attributeCondition on another GCP issuer is MANUAL; a pinned Cognito trust admitting unauthenticated identities is MANUAL; an Azure credential lacking both subject and expression is UNKNOWN; malformed handled facts are UNKNOWN.

analysis.grant_review.description: Emits MANUAL for allowed declared grants classified high impact or broad: AWS non-trust policy statements, GCP owner/editor bindings or classified includedPermissions, assigned Azure role definitions resolved by role GUID, and Kubernetes RBAC rules. It reviews declarations, not effective access; deny policies, inherited grants, runtime conditions and business need remain unresolved.
evaluated: AWS policy documents from PolicyDocument/Document/Policy/policy, supported nested wrappers and policy lists; Statement[].Effect/Action/NotAction/Condition; AssumeRolePolicyDocument is excluded
GCP policy or iamPolicy bindings[].role/condition and resource includedPermissions[]
Bundled offline permission criticality classifier for AWS, GCP, Azure and Kubernetes resource/verb combinations
analysis.grant_review.pass_when: Never emits PASS. No allowed grant with high-or-higher classified severity or broad wildcard/NotAction produces no grant-review finding.
analysis.grant_review.fail_when: Never emits FAIL. Any allowed high-or-higher or broad grant emits MANUAL; non-broad allowed permissions of unknown or partial criticality can separately emit analysis.coverage UNKNOWN.
analysis.grant_review.not_applicable_when: No supported grant declaration exists, the statement is not Allow, or an Azure role definition is unassigned or its assignment cannot be resolved to a collected definition. GCP bindings other than roles/owner or roles/editor are not inferred high impact from the role name alone.

analysis.inactive_identity.description: Emits MANUAL on an IAM_TYPES identity or RBAC resource when its preferred Usage (or fallback usage) object has activity_count equal to zero. This is an observed inactivity signal, not proof access is unnecessary; the reporting window and telemetry completeness are retained as evidence.
evaluated: resource.data.Usage.activity_count, falling back to resource.data.usage.activity_count only when Usage is absent
resource.data.LastUsed/RoleLastUsed/PasswordLastUsed/AccessKeys/activity/signInActivity and snapshot metadata activity/coverage fields as evidence, not as the inactivity predicate
analysis.inactive_identity.pass_when: Never emits PASS. A nonzero or absent activity_count produces no inactivity finding.
analysis.inactive_identity.fail_when: Never emits FAIL. On an IAM_TYPES resource, a dict-valued selected Usage/usage with activity_count == 0 emits MANUAL, regardless of the telemetry completeness value.
analysis.inactive_identity.not_applicable_when: The resource type is outside IAM_TYPES, or the selected Usage/usage object is not a dict or does not have activity_count equal to zero.

analysis.internet_exposure.description: Models declared internet paths or public data sharing for handled AWS, GCP, Azure and Kubernetes assets. For each applicable asset it emits PASS when a decisive collected layer blocks the path, FAIL when modeled ports or public data access remain open without an unresolved decisive layer, and UNKNOWN when the required decision is unresolved. It also emits scope-level UNKNOWN for explicitly present exposure collection statuses outside collected, empty or partial.
evaluated: resource.provider/type and provider-specific public address, endpoint, listener, route, policy and sharing facts for handled assets

AWS instance/ENI public addresses, internet-facing ELB listeners, public RDS/Redshift/OpenSearch/EKS/Lambda/API endpoints, bucket policy/ACL/Block Public Access, RDS snapshot restore attributes, SG/NACL/routes
GCP instance external IP and VPC firewall, forwarding rule/backends/Cloud Armor, Cloud Run/function invoker policy, SQL authorized networks, GKE endpoint, bucket IAM
Azure NIC/public IP, load balancer/application gateway, NSG, App Service access restrictions, AKS, storage public access/network ACLs, SQL firewall
Kubernetes Service type/externalIPs/source ranges/ports and Node external IP; Ingress class/annotations, source ranges, TLS and status.loadBalancer.ingress
snapshot.collections[].scope/type/status for explicitly present EVALUATED exposure collections
analysis.internet_exposure.pass_when: An applicable asset has a modeled collected blocking layer or no exposed ports after its assessed layers, including provider-specific authorization or private endpoint decisions.
analysis.internet_exposure.fail_when: A handled asset has modeled open internet protocol/ports or public data access without an unresolved decisive layer; an attributable foreign RDS snapshot share can explicitly FAIL. Route, NACL or public-IP gaps can remain listed as secondary unresolved evidence without downgrading an otherwise open path.
analysis.internet_exposure.not_applicable_when: A handler returns no assessment because the asset has no applicable public endpoint/share, or the resource type has no handler. Assessed assets with unresolved decisive layers and explicitly present unavailable exposure collection statuses produce UNKNOWN rather than no finding; absent collection entries alone do not trigger the scope-level coverage finding.

analysis.network_review.description: Emits MANUAL for unrestricted-source ingress rule candidates in AWS security groups, enabled GCP ingress firewall allows, Azure NSG inbound allows, and Kubernetes NetworkPolicy ingress rules. It only identifies a rule-layer candidate; attachment, routing, priority, other filters and actual endpoint reachability remain unresolved.
analysis.network_review.pass_when: Never emits PASS. No matching rule candidate produces no network-review finding.
analysis.network_review.fail_when: Never emits FAIL. A rule whose tested source is one of 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0, *, or Internet emits MANUAL; Kubernetes ingress also matches absent/empty from or an empty peer object. Kubernetes ipBlock.except does not suppress the candidate.
analysis.network_review.not_applicable_when: The type is not a supported rule container or no qualifying ingress allow rule exists. For GCP, omitted sourceRanges is treated as public only when neither sourceTags nor sourceServiceAccounts is set; a Kubernetes policy without Ingress in policyTypes or with an empty ingress list yields no candidate.

analysis.principal_exposure.description: Classifies allowed principal declarations from AWS policies, GCP IAM bindings, Kubernetes binding subjects and Azure principalId properties against the scanned/trusted boundary. An unconditional public principal or attributable external principal can FAIL. Restrictive public grants, authenticated Kubernetes groups, unscoped AWS service principals and public grants on network-bound AWS resources receive MANUAL review; unattributable principals yield UNKNOWN. No effective-access simulation is performed.
evaluated: AWS supported policy documents Statement[].Effect/Principal/Condition, including AssumeRolePolicyDocument
Kubernetes subjects[].kind/name/namespace, binding roleRef, collected ClusterRole discovery-only rules, and metadata.namespace
analysis.principal_exposure.pass_when: Never emits PASS. Declarations classified allowlisted or provider_service, skipped source-scoped or trust-policy AWS Service principals, and recognized Kubernetes discovery-only public bindings produce no exposure finding.
analysis.principal_exposure.fail_when: An allowed public principal without an accepted restriction or an attributable external principal produces FAIL, with the public-network-bound exception for vpc_endpoint, efs_file_system and efs_access_point. For GCP, any binding condition moves public to MANUAL; for AWS, only a recognized positive restrictive condition does so. An external principal still FAILs even with an ExternalId condition.
analysis.principal_exposure.not_applicable_when: No supported principal declaration is yielded or every declaration is ignored/trusted. Unattributable principals produce UNKNOWN, and MANUAL applies to restricted public, system:authenticated, unscoped AWS Service, or public network-bound declarations; the overall finding takes FAIL before MANUAL before UNKNOWN when mixed.
